key_insight: Probabilistic trustworthy AI workloads shift bottlenecks from compute to memory because they interleave deterministic data access with heavy, repeated stochastic sampling; treating randomness as a first‑class memory stream enables a unified, more efficient system design.
problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch between conventional memory systems (designed for deterministic data) and emerging probabilistic AI workloads that require high-throughput, low-latency delivery of both data and high-quality randomness while preserving robustness, interpretability, security and privacy.
method: Formalize a unified data‑access model that represents deterministic data and stochastic samples as coexisting memory streams with predictable access patterns.

Propose hardware–software co‑design primitives (e.g., RNG integration at/near memory controllers, entropy-aware caches, and sampling APIs) to deliver randomness alongside data with low latency and controlled quality.
Introduce memory-aware scheduling, caching and security primitives to prioritize interleaved deterministic/stochastic access, audit entropy sources, and reduce contention and leakage.
impact: By reframing randomness as a memory service, the approach helps AI/ML systems scale probabilistic workloads with lower latency, better energy efficiency and stronger operational guarantees for robustness, interpretability and privacy—making trustworthy probabilistic methods more practical in real systems.
visual_elements: Schematic of a memory subsystem showing two coexisting streams: deterministic data and randomness (RNG) delivered from/near memory controllers to models.
Timeline/flow diagram illustrating interleaved deterministic reads and repeated stochastic sampling that create memory contention and shifted bottlenecks.
Before/after comparative chart (latency/throughput/energy qualitative bars) contrasting conventional memory vs. unified memory design (no numeric labels required).
Icon set showing key primitives: RNG chip, cache, scheduler, and security/audit padlock to convey hardware–software integration and trust features.
paper_title: A Unified Memory Perspective for Probabilistic Trustworthy AI
paper_authors: Xueji Zhao, Likai Pei, Jianbo Liu, Kai Ni, Ningyuan Cao
